title: Mosaic Prompt Sculptor — personal jot
content:
Context / intuition:

Quick note: want a lightweight in-browser "sculptor" to assemble multi-part prompts (instructions, grounding, tool calls, safety filters) as reusable mosaic pieces. Focus on helping app engineers iterate on prompt topology and token budget while keeping a small, testable surface for rollouts.

Why: teams building assistants end up with ad-hoc prompt templates scattered across code and environment variables. Hard to reason about token cost vs quality, especially with tool calling and streaming. A small personal-facing UI + dev API that can export a canonical prompt envelope and a compact token estimate should reduce iteration time and make QA/evals easier.

Goals (MVP):
- Let user compose a prompt from discrete components (system, persona, context block, dynamic variables, tool call placeholder, post-processing instructions).
- Show live estimated token usage and cost per model/encoding settings as components are added/expanded.
- Allow saving component library per project and exporting canonical JSON that can be used by runtime (redwood API) or stored in repo.
- Provide a simple A/B switch that can swap in a cheaper quantized variant and show delta in tokens/cost and an estimate of quality risk (heuristic).

Success metrics (initial):
- Time-to-first-working-prompt: median dropped from ~35m -> < 15m for early trial teams (measured via quick survey).
- % of new prompt edits made via sculptor vs raw repo commits in pilot projects: target 40% in month 1.
- Number of saved components per project: > 8 on average (signals reuse).

User stories (raw):
- As an app engineer I want to drag in a "context window" and pin recent user messages so I know what part of the convo is included in each call.
- As an ML engineer I want to simulate a worst-case token blowup when user inputs long attachments and see which components to trim.
- As a product manager I want to preview model outputs for two prompt variants side-by-side with identical seed messages.
- As an ops engineer I want exported prompt JSON to contain stable IDs so rollouts can reference component IDs rather than free text.

Rough acceptance criteria (MVP):
- UI: can create/edit 5 component types, reorder, and toggle inclusion. Save to project.
- Token estimation: uses encoding library and shows both "tokens" and "estimated cost" for selected model family.
- Export: YAML/JSON with component ids, human labels, and compiled envelope matching Redwood runtime input.

Experiment ideas / playbook:
- A/B: enable "economy variant" toggle that will automatically remove lowest-priority components and replace system instruction with a short-form. Measure quality via micro-evals (synthetic prompt set).
- Rollout: start internal with Solutions Eng and 2 customer pilots. Use feature flag by project.
- Telemetry: record component usage frequency, average length per component, and changes between saved versions (for regression detection).

Minimal API sketch (for runtime import):
- POST /prompt-libraries/{project}/compile
  payload: {"library_id": "lib-123", "component_order": ["c1","c2","c5"], "vars": {"user_name": "Ava"}, "model": "redwood/opt-13b"}
  response: {"compiled_text": "---", "token_estimate": 312, "encoding": "cl100k_base"}

- Export format note: include metadata: created_by, component_version, approx_tokens_by_component. Keep schema tiny and stable.

UX flow sketches (thinking aloud):
- left: component palette (system, persona, context, tool placeholder, finalizer)
- main: canvas with stacked blocks, collapsible details, inline token count per block; hover to see sample expansions (when variable bound).
- right: live preview + model dropdown + cost delta; can open side-by-side compare.
- quick actions: "trim to budget X tokens" that runs heuristics (shorten system, summarize context, drop lowest priority context blocks).

Heuristics for trimming (proto):
- mark components with priority score (user-assigned 1-5), trim low-priority first
- auto-summarize: call built-in summarizer on context block if length > threshold
- collapse historical messages into a single compact recap with links to conversation references

Open questions / risks (notes):
- Summarizer quality: poor auto-summarization could cause regressions — need micro-eval gating and rollback.
- Sync with runtime: need stable component IDs and a migration story if team edits library in UI vs repo.
- Security: components can contain secrets? Avoid storing raw secrets in library; provide warnings and redaction.

Dependencies / quick list:
- token encoder library (js) + server-side verification
- small summarization model or hosted summarize endpoint (can be Redwood-hosted cheap model)
- storage: project-scoped metadata in console or S3; lightweight DB mapping for IDs
- telemetry pipeline hook (console) to record component metrics

Next steps / TODO for me:
- mock up minimal wireframe (Figma) by next Tue; share in #devexp and tag Sam/Mika.
- prototype token estimator using cl100k encoder in a simple React sandbox.
- write one-page PRD to hand to frontend + infra (target end of sprint).
- propose pilot projects: "EditorAssist" and "HelpBot" from SE list.

Notes to self: keep the sculptor intentionally brittle in v1 — focus on being useful for iterating prompts rather than covering every edge case. Prioritize speed, transparency (show tokens), and safe export format that can be reviewed in code.

Slack/context links (placeholders):
- convo: #prompt-sculptor
- pilot tracker: JIRA-PI-8423

Random brainlet: small keyboard shortcut to "snap-to-budget" would be delightful. Also consider a CLI that can load the exported json and run a local compile/test harness.

End of jot.
